alert: Tell me whenever ERCOT is doing something abnormal

question.text: Taking everything in this snapshot together, is ERCOT doing something abnormal right now, compared with what is normal for this time of day and season?

episodes.headline: Operating reserves fell sharply
episodes.summary: Operating reserves averaged 11.7 GW and fell to 9.0 GW, down from 17.7 GW the hour before. Net load reached its highest level of the day at 70.8 GW, while batteries discharged 7.8 GW on average, up from 1.0 GW the prior hour.

episodes.headline: Reserves Fell as Battery Discharge Rose
episodes.summary: Batteries discharged 7.8 GW on average, up from 1.4 GW the hour before. Operating reserves averaged 11.5 GW and fell as low as 8.9 GW, down from 17.1 GW the previous hour; net load reached its highest level so far today at 70.4 GW.

episodes.headline: Net load surged as reserves fell
episodes.summary: From 6–8 PM, net load rose from 62.9 GW to a daily high of 72.2 GW as solar averaged 3.9 GW at 7 PM; batteries discharged 9.6 GW. Operating reserves fell from 15.8 GW to 10.1 GW, reaching an 8.9-GW low, while non-spinning reserve prices reached $10/MWh.

episodes.headline: Reserves Tightened as Prices Surged
episodes.summary: From 10 PM to midnight, operating reserves fell from 6.6 GW to 5.6 GW, reaching a 30-day low of 5.4 GW. Non-spinning reserve prices hit a 30-day high of $188/MWh, while the real-time hub average rose from $117/MWh to $193/MWh.

episodes.headline: ERCOT prices surged as reserves fell
episodes.summary: From 7–10 PM, operating reserves fell from 8.3 to 6.7 GW, with the hourly low dropping from 7.0 to 6.4 GW; 7 PM net load was 73.6 GW, the highest in 30 days. By 9–10 PM, real-time prices averaged $261/MWh and peaked at $563/MWh, while non-spinning reserve prices averaged $223/MWh and peaked at $417/MWh, a 30-day high.

episodes.headline: Reserves Fell as Net Load Peaked
episodes.summary: At 7 PM, net load reached 69.6 GW, the highest so far that day, while operating reserves averaged 9.9 GW and fell to 8.0 GW—down from 15.8 GW the hour before. Batteries discharged 9.6 GW, and the real-time price averaged $101/MWh versus a $77/MWh day-ahead price.

episodes.headline: Reserves fell as batteries ramped up
episodes.summary: Operating reserves averaged 12.1 GW and fell to 10.7 GW, down from 16.1 GW the hour before. Batteries discharged 7.1 GW on average, up from 1.9 GW the previous hour.

episodes.headline: Reserves fell as battery discharge rose
episodes.summary: Operating reserves averaged 8.5 GW and fell to 7.1 GW, down from 10.4 GW the hour before. Batteries discharged 3.3 GW on average, up from 1.6 GW; real-time prices averaged $61/MWh versus $37/MWh day-ahead.

episodes.headline: Prices surged as reserves dwindled
episodes.summary: From 7–11 PM, average real-time prices rose from $296/MWh to $534/MWh, reaching $915/MWh—the highest in 30 days—while operating reserves fell from 11.0 GW to 5.7 GW, with a low of 5.4 GW. By 10–11 PM, non-spinning reserve prices averaged $485/MWh and peaked at $845/MWh, the highest in 30 days.

digest: It was a week of repeated evening reserve declines as net load peaked and battery discharge ramped up, with reserves falling to 8.9 GW Saturday and 6.4 GW Sunday. The standout episodes came late Saturday and Wednesday: reserves hit a 30-day low of 5.4 GW, while real-time prices reached $563/MWh Sunday and a 30-day high of $915/MWh Wednesday.
